newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia, China sign live cattle export protocol.
newsitem.headline: Australia, China sign live cattle export protocol.

text.p: A new agreement for Australia to export live cattle to China would produce potentially big returns for cattle producers in Australia's southern states, Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said on Tuesday.

An agreement signed in Canberra on Tuesday by Australian and Chinese government officials to open the trade, represented an important step forward in Australia's trade relations with China, Anderson said in a statement.
Up to 60,000 head of cattle should soon be on their way to China, further expanding a live cattle export industry which had grown by 600 percent since the eaerly 1990s, he said.
Last year alone, exports of Australian cattle generated more than A$300 million for cattle producers, he said.
"This agreement will open doors to a welcome expansion of that trade," Anderson said.
Close relationships already had been forged between China's Animal and Plant Quarantine Inspection Service and the Australian Quarantine and Inspection Service, he said.
This had paid off in the new agreement, he said.
"Once we have firmly established markets in China we can look forward to improving access for Australian products," Anderson said.
The Chinese delegation had now accepted Australia's status in relation to anthrax, he said.
This would permit expansion of the relationship on the basis of Chinese confidence in Australia's animal health status, he said.
Cattle industry bodies welcomed the agreement as a major step in meeting Chinese quarantine concerns.
